messages:
alex: Quick postmortem follow-up thread for the KV-cache fragmentation OOMs. I want to consolidate owners, short timelines, and weekly check-ins here. React with :eyes: if you can take an item.

olivia: I'll take profiling and heap snapshots for the Rust runtime paths. Plan: gather pprof and jemalloc stats for the next 24h load window. :+1:

prashant: I'll pair with Olivia on the traces. Also will add flamegraphs for allocation hot paths.

alex: Great — ownership: Olivia (profiling + baseline), Prashant (flamegraphs + allocation diffs), Sara (limits + canary policy), Dave (GC/allocator tuning + compaction experiments).

sara: Confirmed. For limits I'm going to prototype an adaptive soft limit on per-shard cache size + eviction thresholds. Target PR for config API by EOD Thu (48h).

olivia: Early findings: jemalloc shows large retained extents -> fragmentation. Quick commands I ran:
```
# collect jemalloc stats from process 12345
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics | grep jemalloc
# go pprof alloc_space (where applicable)
GODEBUG=allocfreetrace=1 go test -run Profiling
```
I'll upload raw pprof tarball to the runbook folder in an hour.

prashant: Small note: fragmentation spikes correlate with long-running heavy prefix-cache writes during batch imports. We should throttle batch write concurrency as a short-term mitigation.

alex: Action item list (condensed):
- Olivia: end-to-end heap/profiler artifacts + baseline numbers (24h) -> owner, due: +1d
- Prashant: flamegraphs & alloc diff, propose targeted fixes (48h) -> owner, due: +2d
- Sara: adaptive soft limits + canary rollout plan, alert thresholds (48h) -> owner, due: +2d
- Dave: GC/allocator tuning experiments (compaction, tcache/jemalloc flags), and doc with trade-offs (72h) -> owner, due: +3d
- Alex: Coordinate test harness and schedule weekly check-in, add dashboard panels for fragmentation metrics (metrics + alert runbook) -> owner, due: +2d

dave: For allocator flags, I'll try: --with-jemalloc-mapping ; also plan to test aggressive decay / background purging. Going to run stress example with `memhog` and our sample dataset.

olivia: Pointing out subtlety: the runtime's KV-prefetch path pins large slice lifetimes; a small change in reuse can reduce fragmentation a lot. I'll include allocation stacks that show that.

alex: We should add a short-term guard: on OOM alert, autoscale extra worker then soft-shrink the cache on the next minutely job so we avoid hard crashes. Sara + Dave, coordinate on config knobs for that.

sara: I'll add a config flag `kv_cache.adaptive_shrink` behind feature flag and a canary that only enables on dedicated clusters. Will also add alert: "kv_frag_ratio > 0.6 for 5m" -> paged escalation.

incident-bot: Incident #2026-0319-KV-OOM acknowledged. Postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-0319-kv-oom

prashant: Quick implementation notes: flamegraphs point to `prefix_merge()` and `write_batch()` as allocation hot spots. Two short-term fixes: reuse buffers and reduce copy-on-write during merges. I'll open a draft PR.

olivia: Uploaded pprof -> https://internal-artifacts/redwood/pprof/1763891234/pprof.tar.gz and a small notebook with diffed heatmaps. Summary: retained space 18% > baseline 3%.

alex: Nice — next steps for timeline: weekly check-ins Mon 10am PT. I'll create a recurring calendar and add this thread link. Expected stabilization target: fragmentation < 10% for two rolling days within two weeks.

sara: Canary plan: 5% of traffic on dedicated cluster, run for 48h, monitor kv_frag_ratio, latency P95, and memory RSS. If any of those regresses >10% abort. Will write canary playbook.

dave: After allocator tuning I'll test jemalloc background_threads=1, decay_ms=10000, and aggressive purge on idle. If that reduces RSS variance, we can stage to canary.

prashant: Draft PR created: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4521 — buffer reuse + reduced copies. Running CI stress.

olivia: I pushed a small runtime change that allows enabling compact-on-idle. Requires config: `kv_cache.compact_on_idle=true`. Will gate behind feature flag and limit to clusters with spare headroom.

alex: Good. Please add changelog entries and link runbook updates. I'll own dashboards: panels for jemalloc retained/extents, kv_frag_ratio, rss variance, and allocation hotspots.

sara: PR for adaptive limits: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4532 (WIP). Adding unit tests + integration canary steps.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started to us-east-1-dedicated at 1763920000 for service: inference-kv (flags: compact_on_idle=true feature_flag=adaptive_shrink:true).

olivia: Early canary metrics after 6h: frag_ratio dropped from 0.48 -> 0.32, RSS P95 decreased 12%. No OOMs reported.

prashant: CI stress job (10k concurrent small writes) shows heap allocations reduced by ~40% with buffer reuse. Still working through some races.

alex: Let's keep the cadence: daily quick updates in this thread until stabilization, then move to weekly check-ins. Please prefix updates with "UPDATE:" for easier grep.

sara: UPDATE: adaptive_shrink flag validated in canary, abort threshold configured. Next: roll to 20% if next 24h stable.

dave: UPDATE: jemalloc tuning experiment 3 lowered RSS variance by 18%. Drafting a short doc with numbers and risk matrix.

olivia: UPDATE: uploaded new pprof after PR applied to canary -> retained extents down to 6% at 24h. Link: https://internal-artifacts/redwood/pprof/1763920000/pprof_after.tar.gz

alex: Great progress. Closing loop: will add action item statuses in the runbook and mark completed as we verify. If anyone hits a blocker ping me. :white_check_mark:

sara: Marking "adaptive limits" as in-progress in the runbook.

prashant: PR merged to main branch with buffer reuse. Stress CI green.

olivia: Confirmed canary metrics look stable at 48h. Recommend roll to 50% next.

alex: Thanks team — I'll update the postmortem with remediation status and target next review in two weeks.

sara: Leaving a note for followup: schedule a 2-week retro to check for recurrence patterns (weekday vs heavy-import correlations).

dave: I'll finish the jemalloc doc and add recommended default flags for Dedicated.

alex: Thread complete for now. Will reopen if we see regression. Thanks all. :rocket:
